script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Wednesday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed down nine point three zero percent on the session. Every primary holding finished in the red, and the damage was broad and severe.

Bloom Energy reported earnings growth of six hundred eighty percent year over year. Revenue surged one hundred sixty-six percent. Guidance came up. The stock still fell.

The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady for the fifth consecutive meeting, and markets sold off sharply in response. The S&P 500 declined meaningfully on the session as rate-sensitive and growth-oriented names bore the brunt of investor frustration. The message from the Fed was patience — markets answered with selling.

Bloom Energy is the top story on Wednesday, and the numbers demand attention. The company posted a blowout second quarter — revenue up one hundred sixty-six percent year over year, non-GAAP operating margin expanding to twenty-two point five percent, and earnings growth of six hundred eighty percent. Management raised full-year twenty twenty-six guidance well above analyst expectations. Goldman Sachs projects U.S. data center power demand could more than double, from thirty-one gigawatts in twenty twenty-five to sixty-six gigawatts by twenty twenty-seven. BloombergNEF estimates data centers could account for twenty percent of U.S. electricity consumption by twenty thirty-five. One analyst at Seeking Alpha reiterated a strong buy rating with a price target implying seventy-two percent upside. Despite all of that, Bloom Energy fell one point eight five percent on the session — a classic sell-the-news reaction compounded by broader market weakness. Bears were proven wrong on the fundamentals. The market, at least on Wednesday, did not care.

Applied Optoelectronics was down thirteen point one eight percent on the session — the second-largest single-day loss among primary holdings. A discounted cash flow analysis from Wednesday morning suggested the stock may be trading roughly twenty-six percent below intrinsic value, citing an eleven point five four times return over the past three years. The selloff appears macro and sector-driven rather than company-specific. Watch for any data center spending commentary in the days ahead.

Turning to Redwire Corporation, down nine point two two percent on the session. No company-specific news drove the move. The industrials and space infrastructure sector traded under pressure alongside broader risk-off sentiment. Upcoming government contract announcements remain the key catalyst to monitor.

Over at AST SpaceMobile, down six point two two percent. Scotiabank upgraded the stock during Wednesday's session, calling the valuation a, quote, grey area, while highlighting upcoming satellite launches and commercial partnerships as growth drivers. A Federal Aviation Administration deregulation push — aimed at cutting launch paperwork — was flagged as a structural tailwind for the broader satellite launch ecosystem. Retail sentiment remains constructive, with many characterizing the name as significantly undervalued.

Nebius Group fell twelve point six five percent on the session. Credit default swap costs rose sharply across heavily levered AI infrastructure names, with one report noting borrowing costs reaching levels that historically signal distress. A comparative analysis noted Nebius is scaling at triple-digit revenue growth despite heavy infrastructure spending, while carrying more balance sheet risk than asset-lighter peers. Credit market repricing is the watchdog here.

Bloom Energy, as covered in depth, closed down one point eight five percent despite exceptional fundamental results.

Meanwhile, TeraWulf fell eleven point seven zero percent on the session. A broader story Wednesday flagged former Bitcoin miners pivoting to AI data centers — including TeraWulf — as having shed roughly thirty percent of their value in a single month. The central question now is whether this is a buying opportunity or a structural thesis break. No company-specific catalysts are imminent.

Lumentum Holdings was down seven point six one percent. The optical components sector traded in sympathy with broader technology weakness. Any forward guidance from datacom and telecom customers remains the critical variable for this name.

IREN Limited fell thirteen point six two percent — the steepest single-session decline among all primary holdings on Wednesday. IREN was cited alongside TeraWulf in the data center selloff report, underscoring that the AI infrastructure pivot trade is under significant near-term pressure. No company-specific news emerged separately.

Sandisk Corporation closed down seven point three two percent on the session. The flash storage sector traded lower alongside broader semiconductor weakness. Watch for any enterprise storage demand signals out of major cloud providers in upcoming earnings calls.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, any Federal Reserve speaker appearances following Wednesday's hold decision — commentary on the timeline for future rate cuts will directly affect growth and infrastructure names across this portfolio. Second, monitor credit default swap spreads on AI infrastructure borrowers — Wednesday's spike in those costs drove Nebius Group sharply lower, and further deterioration would pressure the position again. Third, watch for any satellite launch schedule updates from AST SpaceMobile — Scotiabank's upgrade hinged specifically on upcoming launch milestones, and any timing news could move the stock materially.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch the Fed commentary closely — rate trajectory remains the single largest macro variable hanging over every growth name in this portfolio.
